cases.description: When the input byte array is null, encodeBase64String should return null (the underlying encodeBase64 returns null and newStringUsAscii therefore returns null).
An empty byte array should produce an empty Base64 string – no characters, no padding.
One byte (0x00) is encoded to "AA==" – tests the branch where input length % 3 == 1 causing two padding characters.
Two bytes (0x00,0x01) are encoded to "AAE=" – tests the branch where input length % 3 == 2 causing one padding character.
Three bytes (0x00,0x01,0x02) fill a full Base64 quantum, producing "AAEC" with no padding.
Encodes the ASCII string "Hello" (bytes 72,101,108,108,111) to its standard Base64 representation. Verifies normal path without chunking.
A 20‑byte array spans several full Base64 quanta (6 groups) and ends with padding. Ensures internal loops handling multiple iterations work correctly.

Encode a three‑byte array containing values > 127 (Java signed bytes -1, -128, 127). The length is a multiple of 3, so no padding is added. Verifies that the method correctly handles signed byte values.

group: All‑Zero Triple Repetition (no padding, multiple quanta)

cases.description: 30 zero bytes (10 full Base64 quanta). Each triple of zeros encodes to "AAAA"; the final string should be 40 'A' characters with no padding.

Creates a 10 000‑byte array by repeating the pattern 0x01,0x02,0x03. The expected Base64 string length is 13 336 characters (⌈10000/3⌉ × 4) and the final four characters must be "AQ==" (encoding of the single leftover byte 0x01). This tests internal buffer growth and correct handling of a large, non‑chunked payload.

Encodes a 256‑byte array containing every possible byte value. The result should be 344 characters long (86 quanta × 4) with two padding characters. The prefix "AAEC" corresponds to the first three bytes (0,1,2) and the suffix "//8=" corresponds to the last three bytes (253,254,255).

Ensures that for any input the returned string contains only characters from the Base64 alphabet (A‑Z, a‑z, 0‑9, '+', '/') and at most two trailing '=' padding characters. Uses a 57‑byte random payload to exercise multiple encoding blocks.
